title.narrative: Support to small-scale irrigation for increased food production and income generation in Niger

description.narrative:
This project is based on the needs expressed by the local community, the local administration and the recommendations made by the evaluation of the 2011 EA Rehabilitation project. The project will be a response to food insecurity in Baban Tapki area (Maradi Diocese) as it aims at increasing food production, family income and will build on the already existing CADEV-Maradi’s experience in the area.
The project targets 150 families (1050 persons of which 150 men, 150 women, 398 girls and 352 boys) living in 3 villages in Baban Tapki namely Baban Tapki, Garin Sarki Foulani and Dan Chamoua victims of 2010 floods who received support from a previous CI funded EA project. Each beneficiary must have access to cultivable land and be willing to engage in offseason farming.
The project will build 50 wells of 1.4 metres of diameter and whose depth will vary from 7 to 8 metres. The wells will be made of cement rings at 150kg/m3 plus iron bars (6&8mm). The cement rings will be of 1 m of height and will contain small holes to let water in from the sides. Besides building wells, the project will provide water pumps to farmers to help irrigate their farms using water from the wells. A seeds bank (store) to be managed by community members will be built and supplied with essential seeds. It is expected that farmers and the store management committee will continue to run the store for as long as possible to ensure there is no shortage of seeds at one time. Project’s activities will also aim at protecting the environment through the planting of hedges and other best environmental practices. CADEV Niger will work closely with government decentralised services namely agriculture, environmental and hydraulic.
The project will be implemented by CADEV Maradi together with his local network solidarity and development committees (CDS) spread through the diocese. CAFOD Niger Office will play supervisory and support role to ensure that the objectives of the project are being met and essential learning is documented and shared within the wider CAFOD.
A concept note for this project was submitted in October 2012 for IPDF funding and was later approved by the committee.
